benchmark.manualTimeModelSource: Mechanistic token/artifact assumptions; calibrate with local paired tasks

calibrationSources.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
calibrationSources.finding: In a controlled JavaScript HTTP-server task, participants with Copilot completed the task 55.8% faster than the control group.
calibrationSources.limitation: One bounded task does not directly calibrate phase token relevance, review speed, tool overhead, capacity realization, or local ROI.

calibrationSources.title: 2024 Work Trend Index Annual Report: AI at Work Is Here. Now Comes the Hard Part
calibrationSources.finding: In the global survey, 90% of AI users said AI helps them save time; the report combines responses from 31,000 people across 31 countries with labor and Microsoft 365 signals.
calibrationSources.limitation: Self-reported, cross-role survey evidence supplies context, not a causal software-development effect or a numeric model constant.

calibrationSources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
calibrationSources.finding: In a randomized trial, 16 experienced open-source developers completed 246 tasks in mature repositories; allowing early-2025 AI tools increased completion time by 19%.
calibrationSources.limitation: The developers, repositories, and primarily Cursor/Claude toolchain differ from local Copilot sessions. The result guards against an always-positive prior but does not calibrate phase constants.

calibrationSources.title: How Many Words Do We Read per Minute? A Review and Meta-Analysis of Reading Rate
calibrationSources.finding: Across 190 studies and 18,573 participants, average adult English silent reading was 238 words/minute for non-fiction; most adults were between 175 and 300 words/minute.
calibrationSources.limitation: Prose words are not model tokens, and ordinary non-fiction reading is not technical review of plans, research, or validation output. Use this only to challenge rate plausibility pending local timed review.

calibrationSources.title: Observations on Typing from 136 Million Keystrokes
calibrationSources.finding: The online transcription study included 168,000 volunteers and reported 51.56 WPM (SD 20.20), defining one standardized word as five characters.
calibrationSources.limitation: Sentence transcription by self-selected volunteers is not source-code authoring. The rounded 52 WPM mean anchors only the secondary audit typing metric; it directly supports the five-character WPM convention and only contextualizes the 25/40/60 WPM coding range.

calibrationSources.title: Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers
calibrationSources.finding: The U.S. median annual wage for software developers was $133,080 in May 2024.
calibrationSources.limitation: A national median wage is not a fully loaded hourly rate and does not reflect local role mix, seniority, geography, utilization, or overhead. Local finance remains authoritative.

calibrationSources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation - March 2026
calibrationSources.finding: For private-industry workers in March 2026, wages averaged $32.60/hour and benefits $14.01/hour; benefits were 30.1% of total employer compensation.
calibrationSources.limitation: This covers all private-industry workers, not software developers, and excludes organization-specific overhead. Combined with the occupational wage source, it produces the rounded $92/hour example proxy, not an organization-specific loaded rate.

calibrationSources.title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
calibrationSources.finding: Across randomized workplace trials at Microsoft, Accenture, and a Fortune 100 company, 4,867 developers with AI access completed 26.08% more tasks in the pooled analysis (standard error 10.3%); effects varied by experiment and were larger for less-experienced developers.
calibrationSources.limitation: Completed-task throughput is not elapsed-time reduction, phase manual time, or realized economic capacity. The noisy, heterogeneous field effect bounds overall plausibility but does not calibrate any mechanistic constant.

calibrationSources.title: Reading Between the Lines: Modeling User Behavior and Costs in AI-Assisted Programming
calibrationSources.finding: In a lab study of 21 programmers, including post-acceptance work increased mean total verification from 3.96 to 7.03 seconds for initially verified suggestions and from 3.25 to 15.21 seconds (median 6.48) for deferred suggestions; explicit waiting added 2.5 seconds when it occurred.
calibrationSources.limitation: The 7.03-second mean is rounded to the 0.12-minute lower setting and the 15.21-second mean aligns with the 0.25-minute base setting. Suggestion verification is not one general tool execution, and the study does not establish the 0.50-minute upper setting. Local timing remains authoritative.

calibrationSources.title: 40 Years of Designing Code Comprehension Experiments: A Systematic Mapping Study
calibrationSources.finding: The systematic mapping covers 95 source-code comprehension experiments published from 1979 through 2019 and documents substantial diversity in tasks, participants, measures, and designs.
calibrationSources.limitation: The study does not report a transferable tokens-per-minute benchmark and highlights comparability problems. It supports local timed technical review rather than a universal review-rate constant.
